changes.before:
Our employment offices negotiate opportunities abroad for our citizens. Foreign recruitment requests reach us the following day for approval or refusal. Each country may have only §Yone request pending§!, whether sending or receiving.

§YTerms of an Accepted Agreement§!
25,000 people: §G$$10 billion§!, §G25 PP§! and up to §G$$150 million/week§!.
50,000 people: §G$$15 billion§!, §G50 PP§! and up to §G$$250 million/week§!.
100,000 people: §G$$25 billion§!, §G100 PP§! and up to §G$$400 million/week§!.
Population moves abroad permanently. The full payment goes to our treasury. We have no sending cooldown and may negotiate another agreement once the current request is resolved. Only the receiving country enters a §Y60-day cooldown§!, shared across all partners and agreement sizes. Refused or canceled requests move no population or money and fully refund the requester’s Political Power.

§YRemittances§!
Only newly positive net emigration earns income. Outward transfers first offset people recruited from abroad; incoming recruitment proportionally reduces an existing pool. The cap is §Y$$1.2 billion/week§!, with §R0.01% weekly decay§!. Earned income continues after the programme closes.

§YPopulation Transfers§!
25,000 and 50,000 agreements draw from one source state. A 100,000 agreement draws §Y50,000 residents from each of two different source states§!. The entire agreed population is added to one state in the receiving country.
changes.after:
Our labour offices arrange employment abroad for citizens seeking a better wage. Bilateral agreements bring payments to our treasury, while workers overseas send money home to their families.

§YAgreement Proceeds§!
25,000 workers: §G$$10 billion§!, §G25 Political Power§!, up to §G$$150 million/week§!.
50,000 workers: §G$$15 billion§!, §G50 Political Power§!, up to §G$$250 million/week§!.
100,000 workers: §G$$25 billion§!, §G100 Political Power§!, up to §G$$400 million/week§!.

§YRemittances§!
Weekly income is capped at §Y$$1.2 billion§! and declines by §Y0.01% each week§!. New emigrants first offset workers previously recruited from abroad; only further emigration adds remittances. Recruiting workers from abroad reduces existing remittance income proportionally. Income already earned continues after the programme closes.

The foreign government pays the full agreement fee. Workers settle in the receiving country. Each proposal requires our consent; another can be negotiated once it is resolved. The receiving country must wait §Y60 days§! after an agreement before recruiting again. An agreement for 100,000 workers draws 50,000 residents from each of two states; smaller agreements draw from one.

changes.before:
Recruit workers through country-targeted decisions. The sending government may accept or refuse the following day. Agreements transfer real state population and pay the entire sum to the sender. Only the receiving country enters a 60-day cooldown on acceptance. Its arrival report follows one hour later.

25,000 people: 75 PP and $10 billion.
50,000 people: 125 PP and $15 billion.
100,000 people: 200 PP and $25 billion.

The programme cannot be removed while any recorded residents remain. Suspend new recruitment, inspect origin groups and weekly costs, fund integration or prepare repatriation in the Guest Workers decision dossier. Returning the final residents unlocks closure.

Per 1% of the population recorded as guest-worker residents: Healthcare Spending Cost +10%, Bureaucracy Spending Cost +20%, and additional Welfare spending equal to 0.50% of the weekly GDP equivalent. Completed origin-specific programmes reduce these surcharges; ordinary spending on the larger population remains.

Arrivals grant +0.02 Daily Nationalist Support for 180 days and cause a small Stability loss. Stability losses applied directly by arrivals are capped at 3 percentage points per 365 days. The original fixed 5% programme bureaucracy overhead continues until closure. Every 91 days, an active host may face an employer-abuse or anti-immigration incident, with at most one such incident per 365 days. A larger resident population share increases the risk of anti-immigration agitation; completed labour protection reduces incident risks.
changes.after:
Bilateral labour agreements allow our employers to recruit workers abroad. New residents strengthen our workforce, but housing, public services and administration must expand with them.

§YRecruitment Agreements§!
25,000 workers: §R75 Political Power§! and §R$$10 billion§!.
50,000 workers: §R125 Political Power§! and §R$$15 billion§!.
100,000 workers: §R200 Political Power§! and §R$$25 billion§!.
The partner government must approve each proposal. Payment goes to its treasury when the workers settle here. Further recruitment is unavailable for §Y60 days§! after approval. Political Power is refunded if negotiations fail.

§YPublic Services§!
For each §Y1% of our population§! living here under these agreements:
Healthcare costs: §R+10%§!.
Bureaucracy costs: §R+20%§!.
Additional weekly Welfare: §R0.50% of GDP divided by 52§!.
The programme also adds a fixed §R5%§! bureaucracy overhead. Integration programmes reduce the additional costs for participating communities.

§YPolitical Consequences§!
Arrivals increase Daily Nationalist Support by §R+0.02§! for §Y180 days§! and reduce Stability. Stability losses from arrivals cannot exceed §R3 percentage points§! within a 365-day period. Abuse by employers and hostility towards immigrants may provoke further disputes; labour protection reduces these risks.

Manage communities, integration and repatriation under §YGuest Worker Agreements§! in the Decisions tab. Closing recruitment does not end our responsibilities towards residents already here. The programme can be removed only after all guest workers have returned home.
